title: Seven years after seeing YAGA on stage, I finally got to step back in...
transcript: It's 2:30 in the morning, and I just got back from spending basically the entire day celebrating the world premiere of Yaga at TIFF, the new supernatural mystery show coming to crave and AMC plus. And I've been waiting basically seven years for this. Back in 2019, I got to see Kat Sandler's original play. And I remember walking out of the theater thinking, what the hell did I just see? In, like, the best kind of way. It was weird and spooky and funny and sexy and deeply strange. Had this incredibly specific tone where you never knew quite what was real and what was imagination. When it was announced that it was going to be a TV show, I really wondered, like, how do you make this kind of tone work on screen? After watching the first two episodes, I am thrilled to tell you that they nailed it. I'm sure a lot of it is because Cat Sandler adapted the show herself, and she's been working on this show since 2017, so almost a decade. And what's really exciting is that the original play was two hours, and now it's eight, 30 minute episodes, so it's basically doubled in length. And when it was a play, to quote Kat Sandler, there was, like, three actors, two chairs, a table on wheels, and a bunch of paper trees. Yaga filmed in Victoria, and they got to build this entire world. You get to see the forest and the Ocean, the diner and the university. And this strange little coastal town just feels off. But you can't quite figure out why. It's so incredibly vibey. If you like Twin Peaks or folk tales or small town mysteries, dark comedy, or shows where you just wonder if everything that's happening is supernatural, I think you're just gonna eat this one up. Of course, we gotta talk about the cast. Noah Reid plays a private investigator who is brought into the town to look for Henry Park, the son of a billionaire who has mysteriously disappeared. This detective, though, is kind of a mess. He makes decisions that are very questionable. It's hard to tell if he's just, like, a jerk or charming or a genius. He's a complex character, but he has an incredibly interesting dynamic with Clark, who plays Carson, who is a small town police officer, and she does not know what to make of this man, but she is intrigued. And small spoiler, but you find this out very quickly. Hudson Williams plays two characters, but I think we know one of them is Henry Park and the other is Logan. And Logan is Henry's roommate, who mysteriously looks just like him and maybe wants to be him. And then Carrie and Moss as Catherine. She is such a star. She's sexy and brilliant and incredibly compelling. And there's something off about her, but you also understand why everyone feels drawn to her. We only got the First two episodes, but I truly was immersed, and I could not believe that we had to stop there and wait, like, a full month. The first two episodes premiere on October 23rd, and then from there, we'll get a half hour episode each week for the next six weeks. And I am so excited that this is going to be one of the shows that we can talk about week to week, and we can all try to figure out the mystery together, because while I have seen the play, I feel like a lot is going to be expanded upon and changed, and I have theories, and I trust no one. And I can't wait to watch episode three.
